pageCache.pageTitle: SIBFORD GOWER ENDOWED PRIMARY SCHOOL - Sibford Gower Endowed Primary School, Oxfordshire
pageCache.text:
​Welcome to the website of Sibford Gower Endowed Primary School, a member of the Warriner Multi Academy Trust.
​We currently offer wrap-around care from 8a.m until 5.30p.m for children from Reception to Year 6​
Our parents say:“We find the school a very positive environment - the teachers and children (and parents) always look happy at drop off and pick up. All of the staff are so caring and provide a very nurturing environment, always putting the children at the heart of all they do.” “Many thanks to the wonderful teachers at Sibford Gower who have gone out of their way to support my child. I am delighted that he is going to such a brilliant school!” “Thank you for all you do to support my son in school. He is happy and doing well. The school is wonderful and I would highly recommend.” “We’re very happy with the school and the support everyone is very approachable. Everyone at the school knows our child by name, which we believe demonstrates the interest and care the teachers have in the children.” “Our child is in Reception and seems to be exceeding in all areas of education, socially and academically. We are very happy with the standard of education and support the school provides.” “Our child is really happy at the school. We are impressed with the communication with the classroom staff who seem to know him well. Thank you all so much.” "Since coming to Sibford Gower, my children have progressed significantly due to the teachers and staff's care and attention. Thank you""My children feel happy and settled in this lovely school. What a great environment for learning! Thanks to all teachers and staff for making it such a lovely school." “It is refreshing to have teachers and senior staff that genuinely take an interest in the children in school … and really go the extra mile in all activities.” “ I would happily recommend this school.”"Lovely, welcoming, caring, supportive."
Our pupils say:"Learning is fun because we don’t just sit and listen. We learn through games and fun activities.""I like reading because there are a lot of books to choose from. We can get lost in the books and have our own adventures.""I like writing. My teacher supports me if I need help.""I like maths – my teachers explain new learning well so I understand.""My teachers help me by giving me feedback when they mark my work. It helps me improve my learning.""We follow the RESPECT Code. We treat others as we would like to be treated and we listen to each other.""Building learning Power helps us talk about our learning and understand each other when we talk about learning.""The school is massive and very old. The Orchard is beautiful. We are all friends in our school. It is the best school in the world. We have brilliant teachers and amazing teaching assistants. " The headteacher seems like she is very kind. We’ve got well behaved children. This school is the best school in the world !""I love the teachers because they are kind and helpful. I like everything about school and I especially enjoy doing the times tables challenge because it helps my times tables stick in mt head"

Nursery provision at Sibford Gower Primary School
nursery_admission_policy_sibford_gower_september_2025.pdf
sibford_gower_nursery_application.pdf
Nursery Government Funded hoursAll 3 to 4-year-olds in Oxfordshire are eligible for the universal 570 hours free early education. (Universal) There is no need to apply for a code.Working parents may also be eligible for the extended 570 hours for 3 and 4-year old children. (Extended or '30 hours') Information, eligibility criteria and links to apply can be found at Childcare Choices.If parents are eligible for Extended Government Funded Hours, they will be given an 11 digit eligibility code for their child. Once a code has been given, please complete and return to school the ‘Details for Claiming 30 Hours Childcare’ form (available on the school website).You must ensure that you have applied for/re-confirmed your 30-hour code no later than 31st August in order to use it for the Autumn term. This form must be returned to school the term before you wish your child to start claiming Extended Government Funded Hours. ​ All Government Funded Hours are for 38 weeks of the year, for a set number of weeks each term.​

pageCache.text:
Special Educational Needs & Disability (SEND)
​What happens if my child is not making the same progress as other children ?If a child is falling behind, or not responding to inclusive teaching, we will bring together all the information we have about the child’s needs and difficulties and share this with parents. The school uses Oxfordshire County Council’s ‘Identifying and Supporting Educational Needs’ handbook (September 2020) as way of identifying if there is a SEND and what levels of support should be offered. The handbook helps us to make sure we are offering the provision expected from all schools in Oxfordshire. There are four broad areas of SEND:
SEND Code of Practice
Oxfordshire Local Offer
‘identifying_and_supporting_educational_needs’_handbook_september_2020.pdf
Communication and Interaction Needs
Cognition and Learning Needs
Social, Emotional and Mental Health Needs
Sensory and/or physical needs

​Reading Ambassadors
Being a Reading Ambassador is an important role in school. Their role is to model a commitment to reading and to keep the profile of reading high across the school by thinking about ways we can encourage all the children to value reading.These pupils are chosen because they have shown a particularly deep love of reading and a determination to develop their reading ability and/or range of reading interests. ‘Once a Reading Ambassador ALWAYS a Reading Ambassador’ but each year we appoint new ambassadors as older children leave.
Fraser: " Reading improves your vocabulary by a massive amount. With a fiction book, especially if there is lots of description, you can really feel like you are in the character's world.David: "Reading really gives you an increase in your knowledge and your vocabulary"Scarlett: "When you read, you can go all over the world whilst standing still. It's like free magic"Martha: " Bookworms have a bigger brain than other people. The more you read, the more you learn"Molly: "The reading curriculum is important in school. It's educational, good for your vocabulary and it is really magical when you get the perfect book for you"Charlie: "If you don't read, you've missed out on a whole other world"
